claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a characterized hierarchical heterostructure.
The hierarchical heterostructure can be produced using established metallurgical processing.
A physics-informed, machine-learning-enhanced multiscale simulation can use detailed microstructural features as inputs.
Grain-size distribution and phase-boundary character mediate load transfer in HfNbTiVAl10.
Grain-size distribution and phase-boundary character influence crack development in HfNbTiVAl10.
Extracting critical microstructural descriptors and combining them with physics-based information allows the simulation to avoid fully resolving all length scales.
Machine-learning algorithms can rapidly interpolate the mechanical responses of HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed approach will improve prediction speed and accuracy.
The proposed simulation will predict Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture-related metrics more accurately than traditional finite-element or molecular-dynamics simulations.
The proposed simulation will require less computation time than traditional finite-element or molecular-dynamics simulations.
Traditional full-scale finite-element or molecular-dynamics simulations require detailed and time-intensive resolution of the microstructure.
The approach may fail when the material's microstructural heterogeneity falls outside the training-data domain.
The approach may fail when unmodeled defect interactions dominate the mechanical response.
The magnitude of gains in accuracy and speed depends on microstructural variability and testing conditions.
